newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NO FRAUD IN GUN BUYBACK IN QUEENSLAND, SAYS MINISTER

The Federal Administrative Services Minister, David Jull, says to date, a Police investigation has uncovered no issues of concern about the manager of the Queensland guns buyback scheme. A business arm of the Department of Administrative Services won the contract to collect and pay compensation for the illegal weapons in Queensland.
It's been alleged the scheme's manager misappropriated funds and was under investigation for other financial deals.
Mr Jull says the matters are being with the utmost seriousness, but as yet Police are yet to discover any evidence of impropriety.
SUPER LEAGUE DELIVERED BLOW IN SUPREME COURT
The New South Wales Supreme Court has delivered a blow to this weekend's opening round of the breakaway Superleague competition.
The Australian Rugby League went to the Supreme Court seeking a temporary injunction, preventing Jack Elsegood and John Cross playing for the Superleague teams, Canterbury and Penrith, this Sunday.
Justice David Hodgson has ruled in favour of the A-R-L but has ordered it to make a written offer of employment to the players within seven days.
HELFGOTT GIVEN WARM WELCOME IN THE U-S
Australian pianist David Helfgott, whose life was portrayed in the award winning film "Shine", has been given a warm welcome in the United States.
Helfgott, who arrived in Los Angeles today was also given a rousing reception by 300 fellow passengers on his flight from New Zealand.
The passengers burst into applause when the captain announced he was on board just before a screening of Shine.
His first concert, which sold out weeks ago, is in Boston on March he 4th.
HALL FAILS TO HAVE CARELESS RIDING FINE REDUCED
Melbourne Cup winning jockey Greg Hall has failed in his attempt to have a 50-thousand dollar fine for careless riding reduced.
Hall took his case to the racing Appeals Tribunal of New South Wales, over a two-month suspension and fine imposed following the running of the 1996 Golden Slipper at Rosehill.
Hall rode winner Merlene but was reported by stewards for causing interference to several other horses at the entrance to the straight.
The tribunal found that the fine and suspension imposed were correct.
JAPANESE BEEF DELEGATION GREEN LIGHT'S INDUSTRY
The Australian Cattle Council says a trip by a Japanese delegation to beef properties in Australia, has helped shore up Australia's beef markets.
Japanese beef importers have expressed confidence in Australia's beef industry, depite recent fears about diseases such as Anthrax.
Japan is Australia's biggest beef market and one of the most demanding in terms of quality control, but the delegation says Australian beef still has a high reputation.
The Australian Cattle Council paid for the delegation of eight Japanese executives, which examined the industry's safety standards.
AUSSIE TOURISM BOOMING, BUT JAPANESE MARKET SOFTENING
Latest figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics show Australia's tourism industry is booming, with 12 per cent more people coming to Australia last year than in 1995.
Australia notched a record four point two million overseas visitors last year.
While the Japanese market continued to be the main source of tourists -- making up 20 per cent of the market -- growth in the number of Japanese visitors continues to decline.
The number of Japanese visitors rose by four per cent last year, but this compares with Japanese outbound tourism growth of 10 percent.
Our other key tourists were from New Zealand, the United Kingdom, the United States and Korea.
New South wales snared the greatest majority of overseas tourists closely followed by Queensland.
